flagship.headline: Neil Young releases his debut album on his 23rd birthday
flagship.summary_line_1: Neil Young released his self-titled debut solo album on Reprise (RS 6317) on November 12, 1968, his 23rd birthday, per Wikipedia.
flagship.summary_line_2: It was his first record after leaving Buffalo Springfield, and the clip below is The Loner from the album.

events.headline: The Who play the Boston Tea Party
events.summary_line_1: The Who played the Boston Tea Party on November 12, 1969, the second of two nights at the Boston club after November 11, per the Who gig archive.
events.summary_line_2: The band was on the Tommy tour, and the clip below is Pinball Wizard.

events.headline: Neil Young releases his debut album on his 23rd birthday
events.summary_line_1: Neil Young released his self-titled debut solo album on Reprise (RS 6317) on November 12, 1968, his 23rd birthday, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: It was his first record after leaving Buffalo Springfield, and the clip below is The Loner from the album.

events.headline: The Turtles play Happy Together on Ed Sullivan
events.summary_line_1: The Turtles performed Happy Together and She's My Girl on The Ed Sullivan Show on November 12, 1967, per the Ed Sullivan Show site.
events.summary_line_2: It was the band's second and final appearance on the show, and the clip below is Happy Together from that broadcast.

events.headline: The Monkees' debut album hits No. 1
events.summary_line_1: The Monkees' self-titled debut album took the top spot on the Billboard 200 chart dated November 12, 1966, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: It stayed there for 13 weeks, and the clip below is Last Train to Clarksville from the album.

events.headline: Johnny Rivers reaches No. 1 with Poor Side of Town
events.summary_line_1: Johnny Rivers' Poor Side of Town reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart dated November 12, 1966, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: It was the only No. 1 single of his career, and the clip below is the song.

events.headline: The Who play the Duke of York's Barracks in Chelsea
events.summary_line_1: The Who played the Duke of York's Barracks in Chelsea, London, on November 12, 1966, in a session photographed for Getty Images.
events.summary_line_2: The clip below is Substitute, one of the band's 1966 singles.

events.headline: The Rolling Stones play Greensboro
events.summary_line_1: The Rolling Stones played the Greensboro Coliseum in North Carolina on November 12, 1965, per the Wikipedia tour page.
events.summary_line_2: It was one date on their autumn American tour, and the clip below is Get Off Of My Cloud, a single the band released that year.

events.headline: Marvin Gaye releases Hello Broadway
events.summary_line_1: Marvin Gaye's fourth studio album, Hello Broadway, came out on Tamla on November 12, 1964, per AllMusic.
events.summary_line_2: It collects standards and Broadway material, and the clip below is the title track.

events.headline: Shirley Ellis records The Name Game
events.summary_line_1: Shirley Ellis recorded The Name Game, which she wrote with her manager Lincoln Chase, on November 12, 1964, per MPR News.
events.summary_line_2: It reached No. 3 on the Billboard Hot 100, and the clip below is the song.

events.headline: Neil Young writes Sugar Mountain on his 19th birthday
events.summary_line_1: Neil Young wrote Sugar Mountain on his 19th birthday, November 12, 1964, while touring Ontario with his Winnipeg band the Squires, per Wikipedia.
events.summary_line_2: It did not appear on an album until the 1977 compilation Decade, and the clip below is the song.

events.headline: The Beatles' Portsmouth show is postponed
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles' show at the Portsmouth Guildhall on November 12, 1963, was postponed after Paul McCartney fell ill with gastric flu, per the Portsmouth Guildhall.
events.summary_line_2: The show was rescheduled for December 3, and the clip below is She Loves You.

events.headline: The Beatles play the Star-Club in Hamburg
events.summary_line_1: The Beatles played the Star-Club in Hamburg on Monday, November 12, 1962, the 12th night of their second residency there, per the Beatles Bible.
events.summary_line_2: Little Richard shared the bill on some nights of the run, and the clip below is Love Me Do.

events.headline: Brenda Lee sings Fool #1 on Ed Sullivan
events.summary_line_1: Brenda Lee performed Fool #1 and I'm Learning About Love on The Ed Sullivan Show on November 12, 1961, per the Ed Sullivan Show channel.
events.summary_line_2: Fool #1 reached No. 3 on the Billboard Hot 100, and the clip below is that performance.
